summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of idiopathic chronic pancreatitis was admitted for an acute flare characterized by severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, vomiting, and poor oral intake. She was managed with bowel rest, IV fluids, and pain control. Due to inability to advance beyond clear liquids, a PICC line was placed on hospital day 9, and TPN was initiated. Her pain gradually improved, and she remained stable without complications. She was discharged home on TPN with home health support, continuing her baseline medications and follow-up plans with primary care and gastroenterology. Lab monitoring included stable but low WBC and mild anemia, with transient hypophosphatemia corrected during the stay.
